questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: How should you brake?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.explanation: Always start your motorcycle with the transmission in neutral. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the dashboard that turns on when the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This inspection takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, you should care most about the helmet's:
questions.explanation: When buying a helmet, protection is the most important thing to consider.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothing with reflective material to be more visible, even in daylight. Always cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: If you have a passenger on your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride at slower speeds than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A passenger makes the motorcycle heavier, so ride slower and allow more stopping distance. Your passenger should hold onto the passenger handholds or grip your waist securely.

questions.question: When entering a turn, it is best to:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a full stop, let other traffic and pedestrians cross, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are most likely to get into a collision:
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of crashes because that is where your motorcycle and other traffic are most likely to meet.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Why should you change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To prevent a sudden change in power during the turn.
To keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a sudden change in power during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before turning. Shifting during a turn can cause a sudden power change that may make your rear wheel skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show specific traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you move?
questions.explanation: Look through turns by turning only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If you and another vehicle arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go under 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in a way that encourages tailgaters to pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster and more dangerously.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of a small vehicle like a motorcycle. Do not assume larger vehicle drivers can see you or judge your speed correctly.

questions.question: How should you position yourself to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns. Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to hold up your body.

questions.question: What kind of boots or shoes should a rider wear?

options.text: Boots or shoes that end below the ankle.
Boots or shoes that cover the ankle.
Boots or shoes made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots or shoes that cover the ankle.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to dangers.
It prevents you from finding an escape route.
It gives you room to steer your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Space between you and the vehicle ahead gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. This space also lets you steer your motorcycle safely.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to maintain control of a motorcycle in a turn?
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before you enter it. Look in the direction you want to go, lean the motorcycle in that direction, and gently roll on the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time with controlled pressure.
